findings.description: The feature-status table reports 50 requests per layer and elevation and wind generations of 10→1 and 10→6, while the PR body reports 33→35 and 29→38 requests and generations of 9→1 and 9→6 for the same 50-day scenario. The PR body's before-and-after request counts differ, so those runs did not use identical input; their implied savings of 8 and 3 generations conflict with the table's 9 and 4, leaving readers unable to tell which figures support the claim.
findings.title: Overlay savings figures disagree

findings.description: `_refresh()` in `map_overlay_cell_lut_test.gd` sets the private `_map_overlay_last_refresh_msec` directly and then subtracts the interval so `_refresh_map_overlay(false)` becomes due at once. The skip and rebuild counts are therefore checked without the production frame-driven deadline. Only the player smoke test covers the real timing, and only for the biology layer.
findings.title: Overlay unit test skips the real refresh wait

findings.description: `validate_values` now mixes every `wind_x`, `wind_y` and `wind_speed` value of every cell into a hash on each daily climate solve, adding three hash updates per cell to the per-day path. The feature-status record and the PR body report generation and upload counts only, with no measurement of this marker-maintenance cost, so the cost-versus-savings trade-off the ticket asks for cannot be judged. Window frame time is also still pending, so the benefit of the cross-publication marker is unverified on the production path.
findings.title: Wind marker cost goes unmeasured

findings.description: The feature-status entry says the macOS window probe got no draw callbacks, so real frame time and GPU readback are not measured. The only evidence for the gain is headless generation and upload counts. This is the known factory gap: the PR lists it as pending and does not claim a frame-time gain.
findings.title: Window frame time for the overlay skip is untested
